Current auto-start internal=True tasks are separately excluded; that does not make this query defect unreachable because the public task serializer still permits qualifying non-internal signal tasks. Existing single-match tests at tests/test_webhooks.py:1245-1268 do not cover coexistence. Re-saving/replacing the qualifying run or removing the competing match is a workaround, so should_fix.

votes.evidence: products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:41-59 selects the globally newest active matching PR URL before any team/implementation constraint; its branch match similarly selects first at 64-78. TaskRun is a plain model (models.py:1063) with newest-first ordering and non-unique URL/branch indexes (1144-1174), so no implicit tenant scope or uniqueness prevents competing matches. find_signal_implementation_run applies team and implementation checks only after selection at facade/api.py:504-509; it returns None without trying the eligible row. Stamphog treats that None as an absent carve-out at products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:191-200, skipping the requested re-review. A qualifying production run is produced by Inbox's manual Create PR path, which creates a signal-linked task without internal=True and starts its signal-report run at frontend/src/scenes/inbox/inboxTaskKickoffLogic.ts:80-96; the Task internal field defaults False. Another writable task output/branch can shadow it.
votes.refutation: I first checked whether repository scoping, tenant-aware managers, unique references, or the internal-task guard made competing valid matches impossible. Repository scoping exists but does not distinguish teams or task origins; output and branch are caller-writable (presentation/serializers.py:173-180, facade/api.py:2149-2154), and no reference uniqueness exists. Although auto-start tasks are internal, manual Inbox implementations remain eligible, so that separate guard does not make this trigger unreachable. The existing foreign-team test only checks rejection of one foreign match (tests/test_webhooks.py:1286-1311), not selection when an eligible match also exists. Thus a second task referencing the same native PR can silently suppress its review.
